job.title: Maintenance Engineer
job.description:
Maintenance Engineer, Day Shift or Night Shift
Rolleston, Canterbury | Full-time | Day and Night Shift positions available | Hourly rate
A well-established, family-owned timber processing and manufacturing business in Rolleston is looking for hands-on Maintenance Engineers to keep a busy sawmill and processing operation running at full capacity. Two positions are available, one on a Monday to Friday day shift and one on the existing night shift crew, so let us know which pattern suits you best. The site is one of the most automated of its kind in the South Island, with industrial robotics running on the manufacturing lines alongside traditional sawmill plant.
The Role
You'll check, maintain, and repair machinery across the sawmill and processing shed, including plant supporting the site's robotic manufacturing lines, working to a structured preventative maintenance programme and picking up fabrication work on special projects as needed.
Day shift runs Monday to Friday, 6am to 3pm. Night shift joins an established overnight maintenance crew, with the opportunity to grow into a leading-hand role guiding that crew over time.
What You'll Bring
  • A recognised trade qualification (fitter/turner, mechanical, or plant maintenance)
  • Hands-on plant or machinery maintenance experience in an industrial setting
  • Practical fabrication skills for repairs and project work
  • A strong safety mindset, including lock-out/tag-out discipline
  • Willingness and ability to work night shift
Why Apply
Join a stable, long-running operation with genuine variety, hands-on maintenance and fabrication work, and exposure to industrial robotics and modern automated plant most maintenance roles don't offer.
Apply now via the TalentHive website listing.

job.title: Industrial Electrician
job.description:
Join a well-established, family-owned timber processing and manufacturing business based in Rolleston, running one of the most automated production sites of its kind in the South Island. The site runs industrial robotics on its manufacturing lines, alongside PLC-controlled production equipment, giving this role genuine exposure to modern automation rather than just routine maintenance.
The Role
You'll keep production running by maintaining and installing electrical power, control, and automation equipment across the site, including the robotic manufacturing cells. Expect a mix of planned preventative maintenance, breakdown response, and installation/project work, with occasional afterhours callouts.
What You'll Bring
  • Current NZ Electrical Workers Registration Board (EWRB) practising licence
  • Solid industrial or plant maintenance electrical experience
  • Comfort working with, or keenness to learn, PLC, robotics, and automation control systems
  • A practical, safety-first approach and the ability to work under pressure during breakdowns
Why Apply
A rare chance to work hands-on with industrial robotics and automation in a stable, long-established business that's serious about investing in its plant, people and technology, with real scope to build a genuinely future-focused skill set.
Apply now online or call Matt Love-Smith on 0221017007

job.title: Electrical Engineer
job.description:
About the Company
SKOPE is a well-established, family-owned New Zealand company with a global reputation for designing and manufacturing premium commercial refrigeration solutions. Their heritage spans more than 50 years, growing from a small Christchurch factory with 25 staff to a thriving operation of over 300 staff occupying an entire city block.
SKOPE maintains strong partnerships with global refrigeration leaders who share their commitment to innovation and product quality, and is the Australasian distributor of premium Irinox Blast Chillers and ITV Ice Makers. While SKOPE operates on a global level, they remain deeply committed to supporting the local Canterbury community.
About the Opportunity
SKOPE is looking for an experienced Electrical Design Engineer to join their Christchurch Design team. This is a hands-on role, involved from early concept and prototype work through to testing, production release and technical support — working on real products with real manufacturing constraints, alongside people who care about getting things right.
You'll design and improve electrical systems across SKOPE's refrigeration product range: developing schematics and wiring diagrams, supporting prototype builds, testing components and products, helping solve technical issues, and ensuring designs are safe, compliant and practical to build. You'll work closely with SKOPE's design, production, service and offshore manufacturing teams, so clear communication and a practical mindset matter just as much as technical ability.
What You'll Be Doing
Design & Development
  • Plan, conduct and document in-house testing and trialling of components and products to meet functional and standards requirements
  • Design and develop electrical systems for new products and enhance existing refrigeration products, working closely with production teams for ease of manufacture
  • Produce 3D CAD manufacturing drawings of electrical assemblies, wiring diagrams and electrical schematics
  • Carry out electrical wiring and modification work to support prototype and test rig builds
Project Management & Design Control
  • Manage assigned R&D projects to meet time, cost and result targets, coordinating with project team members to hit milestones
  • Maintain accurate records of design processes, decisions and product tests in line with documented procedures
Technical Support & Compliance
  • Provide technical information and support to production, customer service and service technicians — including service bulletins, technical construction files and product specifications
  • Demonstrate a sound understanding of relevant health, safety, electrical and product performance standards, ensuring products carry the required statutory approvals
About You
You'll probably already have solid experience in electrical design, ideally in a manufacturing, product development or similar engineering environment. You'll be someone who:
  • Enjoys practical engineering and problem solving
  • Can move between design work, testing, documentation and hands-on prototype support
  • Understands the importance of safety, compliance and good design control
  • Produces clear electrical schematics, wiring diagrams and manufacturing information
  • Is comfortable using CAD tools
  • Works well with production and service teams, not just other engineers
  • Can manage their own work and follow things through
  • Communicates clearly and doesn't overcomplicate things
Experience with refrigeration would be helpful, but it's not essential. A strong electrical design background, good judgement and a practical approach matter more.
Why This Role?
This is a good fit for someone who wants more than narrow desk-based design work. You'll see your ideas move through build, test and production, with variety, ownership and the chance to contribute to products used every day in demanding commercial environments. You'll be joining a down-to-earth team that values sound thinking, practical solutions, good documentation and doing the job properly.
What's on Offer
  • Work for a respected, family-owned New Zealand company with over 50 years of heritage
  • Genuine ownership across the full product lifecycle — concept, prototype, test, production and support
  • Exposure to new product development within a collaborative design, production and service environment
  • Be part of a company that values community support and gives back to Christchurch
  • Work with premium commercial refrigeration products recognised globally
Ready to Apply?
If you're an electrical design engineer with manufacturing experience who is ready to make a practical, hands-on impact in a growing, globally-recognised New Zealand company, we'd love to hear from you.
Applications will be managed by TalentHive.
For more information, please contact Matt Love-Smith - engineer@talenthive.nz

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
MHM Automation designs and delivers automated systems for the food processing and logistics industries and is proud of its deep New Zealand roots and global reach, operating across five continents as part of Fortifi Food Processing Solutions since 2024.
Our team designs and fabricates customised equipment for dairy, agriculture, timber, grain, and feed industries, combining ISO 9001-accredited quality systems with Lean manufacturing principles and a genuine "can-do" engineering spirit.
The Opportunity
This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role for an engineer looking to continue developing their career in project management, within a genuine engineering and fabrication environment. As Project Manager, you will take ownership of fabrication projects from contract through to installation and handover, coordinating closely with engineering, the workshop, and our suppliers.
This is not a fully desk-bound, spreadsheet focused role, although you will need to be proficient with Microsoft tools. You will be in amongst it: sourcing quotes, raising purchase orders, solving technical problems on the floor, and making the calls that keep a project on track. We are looking for someone progressing in their project management journey with a strong engineering grounding and the right problem solving/can do attitude.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
  • Project Delivery: Manage fabrication projects end to end, from initiation through to completion and handover, keeping schedules, budgets, and specifications on track.
  • Procurement: Source quotes and manage materials, subcontractors, and suppliers. This is a genuine hands-on part of the role.
  • Workshop Support: Act as a technical point of contact for the workshop and stores, helping resolve day-to-day issues as projects move through fabrication.
  • Financial Management: Track project budgets and costs, manage variations, and keep your Estimates at Completion (EACs) current and accurate.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Build strong working relationships with customers, suppliers, and internal teams. Keep everyone informed, with no surprises on progress or risk.
  • Quality & Continuous Improvement: Ensure project deliverables meet our quality standards, capture lessons learned, and complete documentation including as-builts and closeout reports.
  • Safety: Promote a safety-first culture across your project teams, including contractors and suppliers.
What We’re Looking For
Experience & Background
  • A mechanical engineering foundation and tertiary qualification, which could be a trade qualification. Either way this will be coupled with time working closely with the shop floor.
  • Proven experience managing projects, suppliers, and budgets, whether as a Project Engineer, Mechanical Engineer, or in a similar delivery-focused role within a manufacturing or fabrication environment.
  • Comfortable taking ownership of project outcomes with a good degree of autonomy
  • Solid understanding of fabrication, manufacturing processes and materials
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills are essential. Experience with Microsoft Project is an advantage but not essential.
  • This is predominantly an office-based, Christchurch role with minimal site travel.
Attributes & Style
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, comfortable talking with people on the shop floor, suppliers, and customers alike.
  • Self-organised and able to work autonomously. 
  • A practical problem solver who is happy getting into the details when needed
  • Resilient and adaptable, comfortable with variety and a fast-paced, project-driven environment.
Remuneration & Benefits
MHM Automation offers a competitive remuneration package aligned with experience
